svg.title: Full CAD_OpenGL architecture map
svg.desc: Single dense diagram: User events flow into UI, which updates itself or forwards to Scene, the only state-writing layer. Scene submits long work to Shared's worker thread, triggers Analysis, and drives Import/Structure/Orient/Calibrate/Tolerance/Cut, each with its real algorithm steps shown. Rendering reads Scene and UI state reactively and draws.
svg.text: UI — owns camera, panels, sleeps at vsync
UI references a sub-shape → Rendering highlights it
global constants; tool-specific ones live on that tool's panel
Scene — writes a Part's canonical state; orchestrates, doesn't compute
Triggers Analysis automatically after Import or after an Operation commits.
Shared — worker thread, main never blocks
phase-level snapshots only — no continuous mid-call animation
Tools — the Logic layer. Scene invokes and commits; Logic computes. Algorithms below, not just pointers
slices once, shared by all 4 detectors below
threshold: reach distance, not area — far cantilever
is the failure case, not a big-but-shallow area
— warping runs through height, not one face
baseline: revisit time vs cooling threshold
(short edge must be the denominator, or it backwards-
favors long edges) — flag tagged to TopoDS_Face at slice time
minWidth via convex hull + rotating calipers →
weakest axis fails, not average width
open items: raw-pointer rework, uncalibrated NES constants, OCCT boolean cost — see analysis-redesign.md
Logic tool — owns its own Issues cache, keyed by Part. Same pattern as Rendering's picking index, not Scene's
auto-selects faces, user excludes; carve always vertical — never adds an overhang
1. Project face onto its own plane (slanted = tilted, not world XY)
2. Offset by insetMm: outer boundary inward, hole loops outward (untouched)
3. Anchor at each inset-edge midpoint, carrying its inward normal
4. Strut candidates between anchor pairs, validity-filtered
5. Rank pairs: length + normal-alignment + closeness to 45°
(45° is the mechanically optimal bending→axial angle)
6. Land struts on real walls, fuse, notch OUT of footprint
7. Fillet every corner by insetMm (radius = inset, 1:1)
pocket area saved — fill back to solid if skin costs more
9. Cut solid by remaining voids: full Z slab (near-horizontal)
why: bending→axial conversion (truss principle); corners outlast walls by
leverage, not material; fillets cut real stress concentration (2-3×)
automates printer-accuracy tuning; elephant's foot dropped
1. Pick 2 faces: ⊥ build axis (in-plane), ∥ each other
(caliper reading only means something between parallel planes)
2. Classify: Contour or Hole (touches a hole-inner-edge?)
can't mix Contour with Hole — conflates 2 error sources
3. Nominal CAD span = ⊥ distance between the 2 picked planes
4. User measures the print with calipers, enters the value
shrinkage scales proportionally with the part)
elephant's foot cut: different pick shape (2 edges on 1 cap, not 2 faces)
+ it's fixable after the fact via post-processing, unlike Contour/Hole error
open item: raw-pointer rework in CalibDistanceType.hpp
STEP → native BRep, true curved surfaces
off by default; needs a mesh-to-BRep surface-fit
capability that doesn't exist yet — no turnkey OCCT solution
Changes build direction, not the shape —
open question whether it needs an Operation/
history entry, or is purely UI-local state.
algorithm deliberately deferred — separate planned feature
Likely scoped to face-tagging — user marks
reasons about the gap needed between them.
Lighter than tracking relative Part transforms.
source of relative positioning, if it matters.
The one tool allowed to suggest an explicit
fix rather than just flagging a problem —
keyed by Part, owned here — not
on Part, same rule as Analysis's

Reads (never writes): Scene's current Part state, UI's camera, Shared's live-preview slot. OpenGL stays single-threaded — the multithreading need lives in Shared (CPU/OCCT), not here (GPU draw-call volume is too low to benefit from Vulkan).
map, to avoid messy long lines.
